record.original_question: Is it possible to devise a computer program that runs on a modern computer in real time, enumerates all natural solutions of the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph, and thereby generates and determines the general number of all geodetic graphs of diameter d >= 2 that are homeomorphic to the Hoffman-Singleton graph?

evidence.quote: 2. Is it possible to devise a computer program to be run in a modern computer in real time that allows to enumerate the set of all natural solutions of the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with the Hoffman-Singleton graph and to generate and find the general number of all geodetic graphs of diameter d  2 homeomorphic to it as was done for the Petersen graph in [6]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph $G$ is geodetic if between any two vertices there is a unique shortest path. The Hoffman–Singleton graph $H$ is the unique $(7,5)$-Moore graph: it is $7$-regular on $50$ vertices, has diameter $2$ and girth $5$, and is geodetic. A graph $G'$ is said to be homeomorphic to $H$ if $G'$ can be obtained from $H$ by subdividing edges (replacing each edge of $H$ by an internally-disjoint path of some positive length); equivalently, $H$ and $G'$ have isomorphic topological minors with the same underlying topological structure. Assigning to each edge $e$ of $H$ a positive integer variable $x_e$ representing the length of the path replacing $e$, the condition that the resulting subdivision $G'$ is itself geodetic of diameter $d \ge 2$ translates into a finite system of linear Diophantine equations and inequalities in the $175$ variables $\{x_e : e \in E(H)\}$, obtained by requiring that for every odd cycle of length $5$ and every even cycle of length $6$ in $H$ the induced cycle lengths in $G'$ satisfy the appropriate uniqueness-of-geodesic conditions; this is the geodetic system of Diophantine equations associated with $H$ (consisting of $5376$ equations).

Problem. Design an algorithm, executable in practical (real) running time on contemporary computing hardware, that enumerates every positive-integer solution of this geodetic Diophantine system, and thereby produces a complete list and exact count of all geodetic graphs of diameter $d \ge 2$ that are homeomorphic to the Hoffman–Singleton graph.
artifact.status_search_result: Available sources describe the geodetic Diophantine system for the Hoffman–Singleton graph (5376 equations in 175 unknowns) and report only that the existence of geodetic graphs homeomorphic to it has been settled affirmatively (Bosák's problem); no source reports a complete real-time enumeration of all such graphs analogous to what was achieved for the Petersen graph. The full enumeration problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Geodetic Graphs Homeomorphic to a Given Geodetic Graph
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of Bosák on the existence of geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the Hoffman-Singleton graph is settled in the affirmative; the associated system has 5376 equations in 175 unknowns.
status_evidence.claim: Existence is settled, but a complete enumeration of all such homeomorphic geodetic graphs is not reported.

status_evidence.title: The Open Problem of Finding a General Classification of Geodetic Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems in the classification and enumeration of geodetic graphs, including those homeomorphic to Moore graphs such as Hoffman–Singleton.
status_evidence.claim: The enumeration problem for geodetic graphs homeomorphic to the Hoffman–Singleton graph is listed as open.
